To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frog olfactory system is highly sensitive and that the olfactory system is able to detect odorants at concentrations as low as 1 ppb.
the signaling threshold of an ORN is ∼1 pA and that the size of the electrical response triggered by a single successful odorant-binding event is ∼0.03 pA.
(1) the ORN cilium is an extremely sensitive detector of odorant molecules, and that (2) the signaling threshold of an ORN is surprisingly high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) transduce the binding of odorant molecules to olfactory receptor proteins into a signal that is transmitted to the brain.
how olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) transduce chemical information into electrical signals.
understanding how the ORN transduction cascade works at the level of single molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a single odorant molecule binding to a receptor on an ORN is not enough to trigger a signal to the brain, but it takes about 30–40 molecules to do so, and that is a lot less than what was previously believed.

the frog olfactory receptor neuron is the most sensitive known sensory neuron in the vertebrate kingdom, capable of signaling to the brain at a threshold of ∼35 odorant-binding molecules successfully triggering transduction in the ORN.
the ORN signaling threshold is in the range 1.2–1.4 pA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frog ORN is a highly efficient transducer, with an extremely small signal-to-noise ratio of ∼0.03, and a very low signaling threshold.
an ORN can signal to the brain with only a few odorants binding to the receptor proteins during a brief odor pulse.
the frog ORN is a very sensitive detector, with a signaling threshold of ∼35 odorant-binding molecules successfully triggering transduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ORNs have an extraordinarily high sensitivity, which is a key factor in the exquisite sensitivity of olfaction.
, at the level of the ORN, the sensitivity of olfaction is limited by the small size of the physiological responses triggered by a single successful odorant-receptor binding event.
ORNs are very close to the physical limits of sensitivity for chemical signaling.
